heading: Therapeutic Approach
intro: I draw on several evidence-based approaches and use whichever combination suits you and your situation.

items.title: Psychodynamic
items.description: Psychodynamic therapy works on the idea that unconscious processes and past experiences shape the difficulties we face now. Sessions give you space to explore your patterns and defences, and how they affect you today.

items.title: Trauma-Informed
items.description: This approach recognises the part trauma can play in mental health and works with it carefully. Sessions are a safe, honest space, and you decide the pace and direction.

items.title: Systemic
items.description: Systemic therapy looks at unconscious patterns in how we talk and behave, especially in families and relationships. Understanding where those patterns came from makes it easier to change them now. We might use a genogram, a kind of family tree, to map out family dynamics.

items.title: Integrative
items.description: Integrative practice brings together parts of different approaches, such as systemic and humanistic therapy, so the support fits you. Everyone's different, and this lets me adapt as we go.
